title: Response of Teachers to Reappear for TET
body_text:
Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and the recruitment, service  conditions and deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the respective State  Governments and Union Territory Administrations.
The Supreme Court of India, vide its judgment dated 01.09.2025, inter alia, held that the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) is one of the minimum qualifications prescribed under Section 23 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, and is mandatory for appointment as a teacher in schools covered under the Act. The Supreme Court further directed that eligible  teachers shall acquire the prescribed TET qualification within the timeline specified in the judgment.  The order of the Supreme Court may be accessed at the following link:
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/36466/36466_2018_9_1501_63764_Judgement_01-Sep 2025.pdf
Subsequently, while disposing of the review petitions in the matter, vide judgment dated 29.05.2026, the Supreme Court extended the timeline for acquisition of TET qualification from 31.08.2027 to 31.08.2028. The Supreme Court further observed that the respective appropriate Governments/authorities should endeavour to conduct the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) periodically,  preferably twice every year, with an interval of approximately six months between successive  examinations, so as to afford eligible teachers a reasonable opportunity to comply with the prescribed minimum qualification. The judgment dated 29.05.2026 may be accessed at the following link:
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/53434/53434_2025_7_1501_71637_Judgement_29-May 2026.pdf
The Supreme Court, while taking into consideration the practical difficulties faced by in-service teachers recruited prior to the enactment of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, invoked its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and directed that such teachers who have less than five years of service remaining, as on the date of the judgment dated  01.09.2025, may continue in service till attaining the age of superannuation without acquiring the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) qualification. The Supreme Court further clarified that such teachers shall  not be eligible for promotion unless they acquire the prescribed TET qualification.
This information was given by Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary , in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.
***
RRTN

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Ministry of Education stated that per Supreme Court judgments (01.09.2025 and 29.05.2026), the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) is a mandatory minimum qualification under Section 23 of the RTE Act, 2009 for school teacher appointments. The Court extended the deadline for in-service teachers to acquire TET from 31.08.2027 to 31.08.2028, recommended TET be held twice yearly, and used Article 142 powers to exempt pre-RTE-Act teachers with less than five years of service remaining from acquiring TET (though they cannot be promoted without it).
enrichment.context: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 mandates minimum qualifications for teachers, including TET, to ensure quality elementary education as part of India's push for universal, quality schooling under Article 21A. Since education is in the Concurrent List, teacher recruitment and TET conduct fall to State Governments and UTs, though the central government (via NCTE guidelines) sets broad qualification norms. This case reflects ongoing litigation over whether long-serving teachers appointed before TET became mandatory should be retrospectively required to clear it, raising equity concerns for teachers nearing retirement versus the policy goal of ensuring minimum teaching standards. The Supreme Court's invocation of Article 142 (powers to do 'complete justice') to carve out an exception for teachers with less than five years of service reflects judicial balancing between enforcing statutory qualification norms and protecting livelihoods of long-serving educators, while still tying career progression (promotion) to TET compliance.

prelims_questions.question: The Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) is prescribed as a minimum qualification for teachers under which provision?
options: Section 23 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009
The National Council for Teacher Education Act, 1993 alone
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states TET is a minimum qualification prescribed under Section 23 of the RTE Act, 2009, as held by the Supreme Court.

prelims_questions.question: Which constitutional provision empowers the Supreme Court to pass orders necessary for 'complete justice', as invoked in the TET case to exempt certain in-service teachers?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the Supreme Court invoked its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to exempt teachers with less than five years of remaining service from acquiring TET.

Critically examine the Supreme Court's approach in balancing statutory qualification requirements with the service interests of long-serving teachers.
